text_in: On 23 August 2023, members of the BJP staged protests and laid siege to MLA camp offices in Wanaparthy town (Wanaparthy, Telangana) demanding that the BRS-led state government fulfil its pre-election promises which included providing double bedroom houses to the poor and homeless persons, giving an unemployment stipend to the unemployed youth and farm loan waiver to the farmers. Protesters also raised slogans against the state government.

On 19 December 2023, members of the AIDYO including teachers staged a protest in front of the office of the Deputy Commissioner in Dharwad city (Karnataka) demanding the recruitment of teachers on a permanent basis to fill vacant posts. Protesters said that the Union and state governments should take measures to create employment opportunities for youngsters.

On 21 June 2024, members of INC, as part of the party's nationwide agitation, held a protest in the Neemuch district (Madhya Pradesh) demanding the cancellation of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test-(Undergraduate) examination and Supreme Court monitored probe into the claimed irregularities.

On 15 December 2023, candidates, including students, held a protest in front of the JSSC (Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission) office in Ranchi city (Jharkhand) over the cancellation of 85,023 JSSC CGL exam applications.

On 10 November 2023, the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) 2022 qualified candidates gathered and held a protest at the Teacher Recruitment Board Tripura (TRBT) office in Agartala city (West Tripura district, Tripura) demanding immediate recruitment.

On 7 May 2025, teachers under the banner of the Deserving Teachers' Association Rights Forum started a sit-in protest at Salt Lake area in Bidhannagar city (North 24 Parganas district, WB) against the school education department and the school service commission's decision to file review petitions before the Supreme Court, allegedly without consulting them in the 2016 recruitment exercise.

On 26 October 2023, Samajwadi Chatra Sabha (SCS) student leaders staged a protest, raising slogans, and surrounded the Vice chancellor's car, at Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Rohilkhand University in Bareilly city (Uttar Pradesh) over various issues including the delay in admissions for undergraduate law courses, and error in examination results which wrongly showed students as absent, among others.

On 14 June 2024, members of SFI, led by its unit president, staged a protest at the Himachal Pradesh University (HPU) in Shimla city (Himachal Pradesh) over various demands including ending nepotism in teacher recruitment, a central heating system at the library, and the re-introduction of student union elections.

On 16 June 2025, students, joined by the INSO state-in-charge, staged a dharna (sit-in protest) and boycotted exams at the College of Agriculture in Bawal town (Rewari, Haryana) condemning the lathi-charge on protesting students at Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University (HAU) in Hisar on 10 June (coded separately).

On 6 June 2024, students of Dhanamanjuri University (DMU) staged a protest in the administrative block of their university in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding authorities to conduct their delayed examinations and for the prompt removal of the controller of examinations. They withdrew their protest temporarily after receiving assurance from authorities.

On 17 January 2023, Congress activists, including the party's state president and a former MLA staged a protest in Nainital city (Uttarakhand), demanding a CBI inquiry into the recruitment scams under the supervision of the High Court.

On 18 August 2025, hundreds of aspirants held a protest rally in Patna city (Bihar) demanding that the State Teacher Eligibility Test (STET) be conducted before the TRE 4 recruitment examination. Police lathi charged the protesters disperse them.

On 28 September 2024, All Assam Unemployed Association (AAUA) staged a protest and burned the effigy of a Karnataka's Minister (INC party) in North Lakhimpur town (Lakhimpur, Assam) condemning his comments about Assam during an interview and through a Twitter post, stating that Assam lacked the necessary research ecosystem to host semiconductor units and BJP planned to set it up in Gujarat and Assam for political gains. Protesters demanded an apology from him and INC Assam's stand on his statement.

On 21 October 2023, members of the BJP held a protest at Bandra, Vile Parle (Mumbai Suburban - Andheri, Maharashtra), Ghatkopar, and Dahisar areas in Mumbai city (coded separately) against the previous state government led by INC, NCP, and Shiv Sena over introducing and implementing the contractual recruitment system in state government offices. The protestors demanded an apology from the opposition for misleading the people of Maharashtra.

On 3 October 2024, supporters under the aegis of Joint Action Committee and members of IYC picketed, staged protest and held a road blockade at Similiguda town (Koraput district, Odisha) demanding recruitment in government departments on the basis of district.

On 11 March 2023, thousands of JKSSB job candidates were joined by JKNC, JKPDP and DAP leaders including former ministers during a protest and candle-light march at Jammu city (J&K) against the claimed grant of contract to Aptech limited for conduct of various exams as it was blacklisted.

On 14 October 2024, members of the Tamil Nadu MRB (Medical Services Recruitment Board) Nurses Empowerment Association staged protests at the office of the District Collector in Madurai city (Madurai, Tamil Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to regularise their services, fill up nearly 1500 vacancies and provide other benefits.

On 10 September 2024, more than eight thousand guest teachers from across the state gathered under the banner of Guest Teachers Federation, Madhya Pradesh and held a massive protest at Ambedkar Maidan in Bhopal city (Madhya Pradesh) over five major demands including regularization of jobs, 10 marks to be added to Guest Teacher Score Card for experience, a second opportunity to the teachers if they secure less than 30%, conduct a separate departmental eligibility test for recruitment, and implement the annual contract in session 2024 - 2025.

On 4 May 2025, students and their parents staged a dharna (sit-in protest) at a government school located in Scheme No 78 in Indore city (Madhya Pradesh) after power outages disrupted the NEET Examination.

On 20 August 2023, members of the DMK's youth wing protested by staging a one day hunger strike in Krishnagiri city (Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu) demanding the cancellation of the National Eligibility Cum Entrance Test (NEET) for undergraduate medical degree programs.

On 1 September 2025, scores of candidates staged a protest in front of the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) office in Ranchi city (Jharkhand), over the inordinate delay in declaring results of various recruitment examinations.

On 17 December 2023, Junior Engineer (JE) exam 2018 candidates staged an indefinite sit-protest at Eco Park in Lucknow city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding the announcement of the final examination results. The sit-in has continued for 207 days.
On 13 September 2025, members of BRSV staged a protest in Yellandu town (Bhadradri Kothagudem, Telangana) demanding the resignation of the INC-led chief minister over irregularities in exams.

On 23 June 2024, members of IYC, Parivartankari Chhatra Sangathan (student organization), and other groups staged a protest and burned an effigy in Ramnagar town (Nainital, Uttarakhand) against the suspected irregularities in the NEET exams and demanded a fair investigation into the issue.

On 18 September 2024, around 100 people (volunteers from Ladakh), led by a climate activist, on 'Day 18' of their protest march (on foot/ongoing) reached Manali town (Kullu, Himachal Pradesh) as a part of their 'Delhi Chalo Yatra' to demand statehood, extension of the constitution's sixth schedule, early recruitment process along with a public service commission for Ladakh, and separate Lok Sabha seats for Leh and Kargil districts. The protest march has been called by LAB and KDA. The protesters are scheduled to reach New Delhi on 2 October.

On 17 March 2023, hundreds of BJP members, including an MLA, staged a demonstration at the Gun Park in Hyderabad city (Telangana) against the TSPSC paper leak and to demand a judicial probe into the issue. They clashed with police, and were lathi charged, detained and arrested when they were going to attempt to lay siege to the TSPSC office.

On 23 February 2024, thousands of young people (recruitment candidates), including members of NSUI and SCS, staged a protest at the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC) in Lucknow city (Uttar Pradesh) against the suspected irregularities in the Uttar Pradesh Police Constable Recruitment Examination - the protesters claimed that the examination paper was leaked on social media.

On 21 March 2023, dozens of ABVP members held a protest in Jaipur city (Jaipur, Rajasthan) demanding a CBI inquiry into paper leaks, recruitment to vacant posts in state universities, protection from cybercrime, and safety for women, among other issues. Police detained more than a dozen ABVP members when they tried to march toward the CM's residence.

On 15 November 2023, members of the INC's Scheduled Caste department staged a protest on Anna Salai road in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) against the BJP-led union government for reducing the funds meant for the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) which guaranteed work for 100 days for unemployed persons in rural areas.

On 14 October 2024, members of the Tamil Nadu MRB (Medical Services Recruitment Board) Nurses Empowerment Association staged protests at the office of the District Collector in Thoothukudi city (Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to regularise their services, fill up nearly 1500 vacancies and provide other benefits.

On 11 July 2023, students of the Government Medical College staged a protest in Tiruchirappalli city (Tamil Nadu) against the national exist test (NExT) as it would require the students to study 23 subjects in 10 months for exams which would be held daily for six and a half hours over the course of three days.

On 4 October 2023, members of the CPI(M) staged a black flag protest in Kattumannarkoil town (Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu) against the Tamil Nadu Governor for his actions including his support of the concept of Sanatana Dharma (Hindu religious duties) and for not clearing the Bill banning the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) in the state. Police detained as many as 23 protesters.
On 8 January 2024, service selection board job candidates held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) to demand restoration of the provision of preparing waiting lists for recruitment in government services.

On 9 February 2024, supporters of the 'Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra' (Public Rights Journey), a protest march, reached Agra city (Uttar Pradesh) where they blamed the BJP-led central and state governments for the rise in communalism, unemployment, inflation, exploitation of the poor, and corruption. The Yatra which entered 'day 62' on 10 December 2023 began in Bengaluru city under the banner of NBS, RWPI, the Disha Students' Organization, and the Bigul Mazdoor Dasta (labor organization). The yatra is scheduled to conclude in New Delhi on 3 March 2024 - likely to pass through 80 districts across 13 states.

On 10 March 2024, members of the CPI(M) along with various tribal organisations, a Sarpanch and the District Selection Committee (DSC) aspirants staged a one-day 'Adivasi Janarakshana Deeksha' (Adivasi People's Protection Protest) as part of the Manyam bandh in Vijayawada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh), demanding the YSRCP-led state government to implement a government order and reserve all jobs in the scheduled area for members of the tribal community and a special DSC notification for tribal candidates.

On 16 September 2024, e-rickshaw drivers under the banner of the E-Rickshaw Cell of the Berojgar Mazdoor Kisan Union (Unemployed Laborer and Farmer's Union) went on a strike and staged a protest along GT Road in Aligarh city (Uttar Pradesh) against the Municipal Corporation whom the protesters accused of charging tax and confiscating e-rickshaws.

On 10 June 2024, dozens of members of ABVP, including its department coordinator, staged a protest at the Collectorate in Lakhimpur city (Kheri, Uttar Pradesh) against the suspected irregularities in the NEET 2024 results and demanded action against those involved.

On 21 June 2024, members of INC, as part of the party's nationwide agitation, held a protest in the Chhindwara district (Madhya Pradesh) demanding the cancellation of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test-(Undergraduate) examination and Supreme Court monitored probe into the claimed irregularities.

On 31 May 2023, faculty and members of college management, under the banner of Joint Action Committee (JAC) comprising of Aided, Unaided College Management, Principals Association of three state universities and Punjab Chandigarh College Teachers Union (PCCTU), staged protests, outside mutliple colleges in Ludhiana City (Ludhiana East, Punjab) against the state government's decision to implement a centralized admissions portal. The JAC has also boycotted examinations, and Aided and Unaided colleges in the city remained closed.

On 7 September 2023, members of the CPI(M) staged a road roko (block) protest in Kunnam taluk (Perambalur, Tamil Nadu) against the BJP-led Union government for the rise in prices of essential commodities and the increasing unemployment. Protesters demanded the Union government to take measures to control inflation, create job opportunities with social security and increase the allocation under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme.

On 7 September 2023, members of the CPI(M) staged a road roko (block) protest in Pudukkottai town (Pudukkottai, Tamil Nadu) against the BJP-led Union government for the rise in prices of essential commodities and the increasing unemployment. Protesters demanded the Union government to take measures to control inflation, create job opportunities with social security and increase the allocation under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme. Police arrested the protesters - police have arrested more then 1900 protesters across similar protests in the district including in Pudukottai, Aranthangi, Alangudi, Ponnamaravathi, Gandarvakottai and Illupur (coded separately).

On 24 June 2024, members of INC led by the incumbent MLA and Pradesh Congress Committee President held a protest in Kota city (Rajasthan) demanding the cancellation of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test-(Undergraduate) (NEET) examination and Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the claimed irregularities.

On 21 June 2024, members of INC, as part of the party's nationwide agitation, held a protest in the Rewa district (Madhya Pradesh) demanding the cancellation of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test-(Undergraduate) examination and Supreme Court monitored probe into the claimed irregularities.

On 14 October 2024, members of the Tamil Nadu MRB (Medical Services Recruitment Board) Nurses Empowerment Association staged protests at the office of the District Collector in Kallakurichi town (Kallakurichi, Tamil Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to regularise their services, fill up nearly 1500 vacancies and provide other benefits.

On 29 July 2024, candidates who went through recruitment examinations for the various posts in Manipur State Power Distribution Company Limited (MSPDCL) and Manipur State Power Corporation Limited (MSPCL) staged a protest in front of the residence of Manipur's Power Minister in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) for the delay in the announcement of results since 2019.

On 20 February 2024, hundreds of young people (recruitment candidates) staged a protest march in Pilibhit city (Uttar Pradesh) against the suspected irregularities in the Uttar Pradesh Police Constable Recruitment Examination - the protesters claimed that the examination paper was leaked on social media.

On 7 September 2023, members of the CPI(M) staged a road roko (block) protest in Kulithalai municipality (Karur, Tamil Nadu) against the BJP-led Union government for the rise in prices of essential commodities and the increasing unemployment. Protesters demanded the Union government to take measures to control inflation, create job opportunities with social security and increase the allocation under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme.

On 26 November 2024, members of the Tamil Nadu Revenue Officials Association (TNROA) staged a sit-in protest in front of the Collectorate in Thanjavur city (Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu), demanding the DMK-led state government to fulfil their demands which included the recruitment of staff in the newly established districts.

On 7 July 2023, around 100 students and students body leaders from Mizo Zirlai Pawl (Mizo Students Association) and Mizo Students Union staged a demonstration at the legislative assembly secretariat in Aizawl city (Aizawl, Mizoram) against the unfair practices being followed in recruitment for jobs in Mizoram Legislative Assembly, which they claimed was following a route of nepotism.

On 21 March 2025, TSF and Tipra Motha organized a road block protest as a part of the statewide protest and blocked roads in Ambassa town (Dhalai, Tripura) demanding the recognition of the Roman script for Kokborok language and the rescheduling of Kokborok board exams to implement it.

On 28 March 2024, Ladakhi women from the Ladakhi community under the banner of Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance started a 10-day hunger strike at Leh city (Ladakh) to demand statehood for Ladakh, constitutional safeguards, recruitment, job reservation for the youth of Ladakh UT and creation of two separate constituencies for Leh and Kargil.

On 3 January 2024, Patwaris (government registrars) and Kanungo (government clerks), under the banner of Revenue Patwar and Kanungo Association Haryana, on 'day 1' of their '3-day' strike staged a protest in Rohtak city (Haryana) over various demands including recruitment for vacant positions and a hike in salaries.
On 16 January 2023, JKSSB post candidates held a protest at Rajouri city (J&K) to demand that the government hold a fair and transparent recruitment process.

On 1 October 2023, a group of investors affiliated to the Thiruvananthapuram District Unemployed Social Welfare Cooperative Society and members of Left political parties staged a protest in front of an INC leader and former minister's residence in the Sasthamangalam locality in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) after the society failed to return their investments despite repeated demands. Protesters accused the minister of having links with the society.

On 10 June 2024, students and members of ABVP staged a protest at the Kakadev Coaching Mandi (market) in Kanpur city (Kanpur Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) against the suspected irregularities in the NEET 2024 results and demanded a CBI inquiry into the issue.

On 14 January 2024, supporters of the 'Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra' (Public Rights Journey), a protest march, reached Mau city (Uttar Pradesh) where they blamed the BJP-led central and state governments for the rise in communalism, unemployment, inflation, exploitation of the poor, and corruption. The Yatra which entered 'day 36' on 10 December 2023 began in Bengaluru city under the banner of NBS, RWPI, the Disha Students' Organization, and the Bigul Mazdoor Dasta (labor organization). The yatra is scheduled to conclude in New Delhi on 3 March 2024 - likely to pass through 80 districts across 13 states.

On 4 March 2023, contractual and outsourcing employees of Saheed Laxman Nayak Medical College and Hospital (SLN MCH) staged a sit-in protest, as part of a relay strike, in front of the Hospital in Koraput town (Koraput, Odisha) claiming corruption in recruitment of permanent staff.

On 21 June 2024, hundreds of INC supporters staged a protest as a part of the nationwide protest called by All India Congress Committee with chants, slogans and burned the effigy of Union Education Minister at Congress Bhavan in Agartala city (West Tripura, Tripura) over irregularities found during the recent National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) Under Graduate 2024 and the cancellation of National Eligibility Test (NET) examination. Protesters demanded the resignation of Union Education Minister and for the examinations to be conducted again.

On 1 August 2024, KSU activists staged a protest and burned copies of Meghalaya Public Service Commission's (MPSC) reply to KSU addressing the grievances they presented against the civil service recruitment processes in Shillong city (East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya) and condemned it.

On 14 October 2024, members of the Tamil Nadu MRB (Medical Services Recruitment Board) Nurses Empowerment Association staged protests at the office of the District Collector in Tiruvannamalai city (Tiruvannamalai, Tamil Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to regularise their services, fill up nearly 1500 vacancies and provide other benefits.

On 8 January 2025, ABSU and prominent Bodo organizations including Bodo Sahitya Sabha, Bodo Samaj, Harimu Afad (cultural organisation), All Assam Tribal Sangha, and All Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR) Venture Senior Secondary School Employees' Association staged a protest in all the district headquarters of Assam including Sonari town (Charaideo, Assam) with 6 demands including the inclusion of the Bodo language in the Assam Judicial Service Examinations and Central Teacher Eligibility Test (CTET), the establishment of 35 new Bodo medium high schools, the provincialization of Venture Schools under Clause 6.3 of the BTR Accord, the filling of vacant spots and dropout positions in Bodo medium schools along with the recruitment of teachers and upgradation of 101 Bodo medium high schools to higher secondary schools.

On 14 October 2024, members of the Tamil Nadu MRB (Medical Services Recruitment Board) Nurses Empowerment Association staged protests at the office of the District Collector in Coimbatore city (Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to regularise their services, fill up nearly 1500 vacancies and provide other benefits.

Around 12 April 2025 (as reported), over a hundred locals staged a protest in Dalgaon town (Darrang, Assam) demanding the resignation of Konaktapara Higher Secondary School's Headmaster and School Management Committee (SMC) President over negligence after only 5 students passed the High School Leaving Certificate (HSLC) examination out of 36 students.

On 4 April 2025, BJP members held a protest at Chinsurah city (Hooghly district, WB) against claimed irregularities in recruitment of teachers and non-teaching staff employees by the state government.

On 21 June 2024, members of INC, as part of the party's nationwide agitation, held a protest in the Betul district (Madhya Pradesh) demanding the cancellation of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test-(Undergraduate) examination and Supreme Court monitored probe into the claimed irregularities.

On 7 March 2023, thousands of members of the All Arunachal Pradesh Students Union, parents, and senior politicians staged a demonstration march in Itanagar city (Papum Pare, Arunachal Pradesh). They demanded the government rollback its decision to declare all exams hosted by the Arunachal Pradesh Civil Service Commission as 'null and void' since 2014. They raised concern that such policy would also punish the innocent.

On 10 December 2024, CPI members including a former minister, a former MLA and AITUC's President staged a protest near Swadeshi Mills in Puducherry city (Puducherry) condemning the rise in prices of essential goods and unemployment, then demanded a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) to investigate the bribery accusations against the Adani group and discussions about the Manipur crisis in the Parliament.
On 9 October 2023, students staged a protest march at Kurukshetra University in Kurukshetra city (Haryana) against the examination branch for failing to announce and distribute results on time.

On 3 October 2023, BJP members led by ministers held a protest march at Kolkata city (WB) over an increase in dengue cases and claimed irregularities in the recruitment process for government employees.

On 15 June 2024, members of the KSU staged a protest in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) demanding the BJP-led Union government to cancel the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) over allegations of malpractice and corruption. The protesters also demanded in investigation into allegations of irregularities by the National Testing Agency (NTA) which conducted the NEET exam.

On 20 November 2023, a group of students of Maharaja's college under the aegis of the AIDSO staged a protest in Mysuru city (Karnataka) demanding the appointment of teaching faculty. Protesters also demanded the administration to postpone exams, and to be given access to the college facilities. Protesters also submitted a memorandum to the vice-chancellor.

On 21 June 2024, members of INC, as part of the party's nationwide agitation, held a protest in the Shahdol district (Madhya Pradesh) demanding the cancellation of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test-(Undergraduate) examination and Supreme Court monitored probe into the claimed irregularities.

On 10 February 2023, a group of people staged a protest in Kotdwara city (Pauri Garhwal district, Uttarakhand), against the government. They demanded an inquiry by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) into the alleged paper leaks and government job recruitment scams in Uttarakhand.

On 18 January 2024, hundreds of job aspirants staged a protest in Bhubaneswar city (Khorda, Odisha) over irregularities in junior teacher recruitment conducted by the Odisha School Education Programme Authority (OSEPA).

On 26 March 2025, physical education teachers held a protest march toward the Gujarat Assembly in Gandhinagar city (Gujarat), demanding permanent recruitment and job security. The police detained them before they could reach gate no. 1.

On 21 June 2024, INC and NSUI members staged a protest, raising slogans, and burned an effigy at Gola Park in Srinagar city (Pauri Garhwal, Uttarakhand) against the suspected irregularities in the NEET exams and demanded a CBI inquiry into the issue.

On 27 February 2023, hundreds of MPPSC aspirants staged a sit-in protest outside the MPPSCs office in the Indore city (Indore, Madhya Pradesh) demanding the interviews of State Dental Surgeon 2021, State Engineering Examination-2021, State Assistant Management Examination-2021, and State Veterinary Assistant Surgeon 2021 at the earliest.

On 11 December 2023, members of the BJP, led by the BJP Leader of Opposition in the State Assembly and the BJP State president, staged an 'Aakrosh Diwas' (anger day) protest, carrying empty utensils and fertilizer bags, in Shimla city (Himachal Pradesh) against the INC-led state government whom the protesters accused of failing to resolve various issues including inflation and unemployment. The protest was part of a state-wide protest.

On 29 November 2024, 6 student organizations including SFI and DYFI staged a protest at Dighalipukhuri locality in Guwahati city (Kamrup Metropolitan, Assam) demanding the withdrawal of the draft rules for Assam's college teacher recruitment process claiming that it would take away autonomy from colleges.

On 11 June 2024, members of INC, led by its metropolitan president, staged a protest, raising slogans, and burned effigies at DD Chowk (intersection) in Rudrapur city (Udham Singh Nagar, Uttarakhand) over various issues including the increase in milk prices, toll tax and the suspected irregularities in the NEET 2024 results.

On 25 September 2024, many SP members and leaders, led by its district president, staged a protest at the Collectorate in Meerut city (Uttar Pradesh) over various issues including the rising crime rate, unemployment, and inflation.
On 3 February 2023, a group of students staged a protest in Pune city (Pune, Maharashtra) demanding the implementation of a newly introduced pattern for the MPSC examination (Main) from 2023.

On 13 June 2024, National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) aspirants and NSUI members staged a protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi - Connaught Place (New Delhi, Delhi) against the suspected irregularities in the NEET 2024 results and demanded an inquiry into the issue and a re-examination.

On 7 February 2023, dozens of protesters gathered under the aegis of Berojgar Ekikrat Mahasangh and held a protest outside the RPSC office in Ajmer city (Ajmer, Rajasthan) demanding a CBI investigation of a paper leak incident. Police used mild force (baton-charge) to control the mob and arrested two protestors.
On 13 January 2023, MPSC aspirants staged a protest in Aurangabad city (Aurangabad, Maharashtra) against the newly introduced pattern for the MPSC examination (Main).

On 20 May 2024, 181 job aspirants from families who were evicted for the construction of the Vallarpadam container trans-shipment terminal, under the aegis of the Moolamppilly Coordination Committee (MCC) staged a protest in in front of the district collectorate in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) demanding the government to honour the promise of granting the evictees government jobs. The protesters submitted job applications to mark their protest.

On 3 October 2025, scores of fire and emergency services job aspirants held a protest at Srinagar city (J&K) over claimed large-scale irregularities in a recruitment process pending for more than a decade.

On 24 June 2024, Chatra Mukti Sangram Samiti (students' body) staged a protest and burned the effigy of Union Home Minister at National highway 37, Demow Chariali in Demow town (Sivasagar, Assam) over irregularities found in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) Under Graduate 2024 examination, National Eligibility Test (NET) examination and inconvenience faced by students with 'Samarth' portal.

On 1 October 2024, fireman candidates staged a protest march 'Day 3', bare-bodied and raised slogans, in Rohtak city (Haryana) demanding appointment letters for candidates who had passed the mains exams. The protesters started their march on 29 September from Rewari (coded separately).

Around 31 August 2025 (as reported), students staged a protest outside the vice-chancellor's office at Nagpur University in Nagpur city (Maharashtra) over incorrect marking in the evaluation of their summer exam papers.

On 16 September 2023, members of INC marked the Prime Minister's birthday as 'National Unemployment Day' and staged a protest in Agartala city (West Tripura district, Tripura) demanding employment to the youth.

On 7 July 2025, students, including NSUI members, staged a protest, and raised slogans at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University in Agra city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding special examinations and grace marks for undergraduate students who had failed their examinations. The protesters also broke the lock of the secretariat since no university officials were available to hear their demands.

On 7 September 2023, members of the CPI(M) staged a road roko (block) protest in front of the Head Post Office in Thoothukudi city (Tamil Nadu) against the BJP-led Union government for the rise in prices of essential commodities, the increasing unemployment and anti-people policies. Police arrested 600 protesters including 213 women across similar protests Toothukudi district including in Thoothukudi, Tiruchendur, Kovilpatti and Srivaikundam (coded separately)

On 11 March 2024, students under the aegis of Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) and All Jharkhand Students Union (AJSU), held a protest and locked the Ranchi University (RU) campus gates in Ranchi city (Jharkhand) claiming irregularities in the holding of semester IV examinations.

On 6 August 2024, police detained 181 government job aspirants out of 500-700 who were on their 2nd day of protest at Ram Katha Maidan in Gandhinagar city (Gujarat) demanding the abolition of the Computer based Recruitment Test (CBRT) method in the recruitment exam for the post of Forest Beat Guard.

On 26 February 2024, hundreds of examination candidates, holding placards, staged a protest near the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC) office in Allahabad city (Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh) against the suspected irregularities in the Uttar Pradesh Police Constable Recruitment Examination - the protesters claimed that the examination paper was leaked on social media.

On 20 August 2023, members of the DMK's youth wing protested by staging a one day hunger strike in Tiruvannamalai city (Tiruvannamalai, Tamil Nadu) demanding the cancellation of the National Eligibility Cum Entrance Test (NEET) for undergraduate medical degree programs.

On 21 June 2024, INC members and leaders, including the INC farmer district president, and the minority state secretary, led by its district president, staged a protest at the Collectorate in Kannauj city (Uttar Pradesh) against the suspected irregularities in the NEET exams. The protest was part of a nationwide protest called by the All India Congress Committee (AICC).

On 7 February 2025, villagers held a protest by blocking the Dhenkanal-Cuttack highway for half an hour in Dhenkanal district (Odisha) demanding a proper investigation after a 16-year-old girl committed suicide due to exam pressure.

Around 7 February 2024 (as reported), members of the Jharkhand State Students' Union (JSSU) held a protest in Saraikela city (Seraikela Kharsawan district, Jharkhand) demanding a CBI probe into the JSSC paper leak.

On 14 August 2024, medical students along with a TDP MP staged a protest by taking out a candlelight march at the Apollo Institute of Medical Sciences and Research (AIMSR) in Chittoor city (Andhra Pradesh) to condemn the Kolkata doctor rape-murder case where an on-duty trainee doctor was raped and murdered at the R.G.
